Researcher in Theoretical Physics

Quantum aspects of cosmology and astrophysics from Cambridge to Kraków , sharing news, research and resources…

Doctor who?

As a Brittany-born Norman French , I was perhaps fated for problems from the start. I spent the first 20 years of my life in Nantes, France, the steampunk city of the North West. My first encounter with space, and most importantly cosmology, was unfortunately NOT while watching the stars, an apple falling from a tree, a rocket launching, or while reading S. Hawking’s A Brief History of Time. I like learning and that is about all you need to know.

After realising that zookeeper was not my destiny, that heart surgeon would take too long to study, and that politics… well, anyway, I decided to do something involving maths. Maths were comforting and felt right, until the existential overdose when I realised that maybe I liked it mainly as a tool to answer ‘day-to-day’ questions. I had a great time doing Physics in a Grande Ecole in Paris, followed by a master’s in Cambridge. I started my academic research journey at the former, where I worked on reconstructing the quantum structure of crystals. In Cambridge, I started looking into theoretical physics, and eventually my own series of why? questions converged (or diverged?) towards asking how? about the whole thing (more commonly called the Universe).

In the past 4 years, I studied the early, fast-expanding universe by extending Einstein’s equations of General Relativity to fluctuations generated by the quantum vacuum. In this process, I also looked at the classicalisation of spacetime and have produced and run cutting-edge simulations of the inflating universe (and still do). Pen, paper and supercomputer is a lovely routine of mine.

I am currently transiting from my PhD in Cambridge to a postdoctoral position in Kraków , where I will continue to study quantum corrections to gravitational physics but in a different context: stay tuned!

Publications

Stochastic scalar-tensor inflation and beyond
Y. Launay · arXiv preprint · 2026-06-05
Extends the stochastic formalism for how quantum vacuum fluctuations become classical during inflation to scalar-tensor theories, covering Gauss-Bonnet, generalized Brans-Dicke, Horndeski and braiding theories, plus multifield coarse-graining in full General Relativity.
Preprint
CosmologyInflationStochastic Methods
Stochastic Inflation in Numerical Relativity
Y. L. Launay, G. I. Rigopoulos, E. P. S. Shellard · Physical Review D 113 (12), 123515 (2026) · 2025-12-16
Re-derives the 3+1 stochastic inflation equations in a gauge-invariant manner and implements them numerically in the BSSN formulation, showing correct evolution and well-satisfied constraints for slow-roll and ultra-slow-roll scenarios.
PreprintArticle
CosmologyNumerical RelativityStochastic Methods
Fairness-Aware Test-Time Prompt Tuning
Y. Launay, P. Kamalaruban, T. Kempton, S. Burrell, D. Sutton · Machine learning conference submission (Featurespace placement, 2025)
A test-time prompt tuning method for improving fairness in language model outputs without retraining the underlying model, developed during a machine learning placement at Featurespace.
Preprint
Machine LearningFairness
DMAP: A Distribution Map for Text
T. Kempton, J. Rozanova, P. Kamalaruban, M. Madigan, K. Wresilo, Y. L. Launay, D. Sutton, S. Burrell · International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR) 2026 · 2026-02-12
A technique that maps text, via a language model, to samples encoding rank and probability information, used to validate generation parameters, analyse synthetic-text detection, and uncover statistical patterns in models trained on artificial data.
PreprintArticle
Machine LearningNLP
Bunch-Davies initial conditions and non-perturbative inflationary dynamics in Numerical Relativity
Y. L. Launay, G. I. Rigopoulos, E. P. S. Shellard · Physical Review D 112 (4), 043518 (2025) · 2025-02-10
Shows that realistic inhomogeneities during inflation can be simulated with Numerical Relativity from stochastic Bunch-Davies-consistent initial conditions, across a quadratic potential, an inflection-point potential, and a strong resonance model.
PreprintArticle
CosmologyNumerical Relativity
Quantitative classicality in cosmological interactions during inflation
Y. L. Launay, G. I. Rigopoulos, E. P. S. Shellard · Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics 2025 (05), 071 · 2024-12-20
Introduces a quantitative 'quantum interactivity' measure for when classical descriptions of inflationary perturbations suffice, showing non-linear contributions can be accurately described classically even before horizon crossing.
PreprintArticle
CosmologyInflation
Stochastic Inflation in General Relativity
Y. L. Launay, G. I. Rigopoulos, E. P. S. Shellard · Physical Review D 109 (12), 123523 (2024) · 2024-01-16
Presents a framework for stochastic inflation using complete General Relativity, deriving gauge-invariant Langevin source terms for the Einstein equations in ADM and BSSN formulations, enabling numerical relativity simulations.
PreprintArticle
CosmologyInflationStochastic Methods
N-representable one-electron reduced density matrices reconstruction at non-zero temperatures
Y. Launay, J.-M. Gillet · Acta Crystallographica Section B: Structural Science, Crystal Engineering and Materials 77 (5), 683-694 · 2021
Reconstructs one-electron reduced density matrices from X-ray structure factors and Compton profiles while accounting for atomic thermal motion, using Semi-Definite Programming to recover static, N-representable matrices from experimental data at non-zero temperature.
Article
